edits.text: PRELIMINARY STATEMENT. Defendant responds to Plaintiff’s First Requests for Production subject to the specific objections and responses stated below. Defendant’s responses are based on information reasonably available at this time and are not an admission concerning the existence, relevance, or admissibility of any document.

1. GENERAL OBJECTIONS. Defendant objects to each request to the extent it seeks information protected from disclosure by the attorney-client privilege, work-product doctrine, or any other applicable protection. Defendant further objects to any request to the extent it is vague, ambiguous, overbroad, unduly burdensome, or seeks information that is not relevant or proportional to the needs of the case. These objections are asserted only to the extent applicable to a particular request and do not expand the scope of any response.

2. PRODUCTION. Subject to and without waiving applicable objections, Defendant will produce non-privileged documents responsive to the requests after a reasonable search, to the extent such documents are in Defendant’s possession, custody, or control. Any response limiting production will identify the limitation applicable to that request.

3. PRIVILEGE LOG. To the extent Defendant withholds responsive documents on the basis of privilege or work-product protection, Defendant will provide information sufficient to assess the claim, consistent with applicable law and any agreement of the parties. The parties may meet and confer regarding the form and timing of any privilege log.

4. RESERVATION. Defendant reserves the right to supplement or amend these responses as permitted by the applicable rules and based on information subsequently obtained. This reservation does not relieve Defendant of any obligation imposed by those rules.

Regards,
